implementation_notes: The idiomatic Scala realization does not lock the cluster at all: give the aggregate its own actor (Akka/Pekko typed, cluster sharding entity per cluster id) and let the mailbox serialize access - the Akka documentation states that no synchronized or AtomicInteger guards are needed because an actor instance processes one message at a time. That single-writer illusion is the same guarantee the coarse-grained lock provides, expressed as ownership instead of acquisition, and it removes lock ordering, timeouts and stale locks in one process. Persistence still needs its own guard: the actor's command handler runs the version bump or SELECT ... FOR UPDATE inside one transaction before replying.
idiom_name: actor per aggregate: single-writer ownership replaces the cluster lock
code_sketch:
sealed trait Cmd
final case class AddLine(replyTo: ActorRef[Done], line: Line) extends Cmd

// one entity per aggregate root; the mailbox serialises the cluster
val entity: ActorRef[Cmd] =
  sharding.entityRefFor(OrderTypeKey, orderId.toString)
entity ! AddLine(replyTo = self, line = line)
// handlers run one at a time -> no locks around root or members
pitfalls: An actor only serializes while it is the sole owner: giving out a reference to the mutable aggregate (or running blocking I/O in the handler and touching state from a future callback) reintroduces the races the mailbox was hiding.

Cluster sharding is per cluster id but not per process: during rebalancing two incarnations may exist briefly, so the durable write still needs a version check or row lock rather than relying on single-writer alone.
